narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 19% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reason the model reached this decision is that you haven’t failed any classes before—this actually works in your favor, lowering the risk of failing this year. However, two other key factors are pulling the prediction the other way. First, your father’s education level is secondary school, which the model sees as slightly increasing the risk compared to students whose fathers have higher qualifications. Second, you’ve said you want to go on to higher education, and while this ambition is great, the model interprets it as a small signal that you might be at higher risk, possibly because students with big academic goals sometimes struggle if their current habits don’t match their aspirations.

Other details, like your study time being less than two hours a week and not having internet at home, also played a role, though they weren’t the strongest influences. The good news is that many of these factors can change. The remedial courses will give you structured time to build stronger study habits, and small adjustments—like increasing your weekly study hours or finding ways to access online resources—could make a real difference. The goal isn’t just to pass this year, but to set you up for the future you’re aiming for.
